evidence.quote: Problem 6.1.3 Let Ω be a smooth bounded planar domain and let T : L2 (Ω) 7→ L2 (Ω) be the Kohn solution operator for ∂/∂ z̄. For h ∈ L∞ (Ω) we define the compact non-self-adjoint operator Sh : L2 (Ω) 7→ L2 (Ω), f 7→ h̄T f . Under what circumstance will Sh have eigenvalues? Consider in particular the case where h is holomorphic. If h has a single-valued holomorphic primitive H then it is not hard to see that Sh has no eigenvalues. (Just note that e−H̄/λ T f is holomorphic and orthogonal to holomorphic functions.) Does the converse hold? That is: do periods of H guarantee the existence of eigenvalues? evidence.quote: Problem 10.2.2 The Fatou Set of a Polynomial Automorphism of C2 . Let f be a polynomial automorphism of C2 , and suppose that f is not conjugate to an elementary map. Let Ω be a connected component of the set of points where the forward iterates {f n : n = 1, 2, 3, ...} are locally bounded, which is the Fatou set of f . Let us suppose that Ω is periodic, i.e. f n Ω = Ω for some n 6= 0. Let us first consider the case in which Ω is recurrent, i.e. Ω contains a point whose orbit does not converge to ∂Ω. In this case Ω is either (a) a basin of attraction of a sink orbit, (b) the basin of attractin of a Siegel disk, or (c) the basin of a Herman ring. It is not hard to construct examples of (a) and (b). (i) Can case (c) occur? Nothing at all seems to be known about periodic domains which are not recurrent. (iii) If Ω is not recurrent, does there exist P ∈ ∂Ω such that f n P = P , and one of the eigenvalues of DF (P ) is e2πip/q ? -E. Bedford, bedford@iubacs.bitnet or bedford@ucs.indiana.edu.

accepted.question_text: The Fatou Set of a Polynomial Automorphism of C^2 . Let f be a polynomial automorphism of C^2 , and suppose that f is not conjugate to an elementary map. Let Omega be a connected component of the set of points where the forward iterates {f n : n = 1, 2, 3, ...} are locally bounded, which is the Fatou set of f . Let us suppose that Omega is periodic, i.e. f n Omega = Omega for some n 6= 0. Let us first consider the case in which Omega is recurrent, i.e. Omega contains a point whose orbit does not converge to ∂Omega. In this case Omega is either (a) a basin of attraction of a sink orbit, (b) the basin of attractin of a Siegel disk, or (c) the basin of a Herman ring. It is not hard to construct examples of (a) and (b). (i) Can case (c) occur? Nothing at all seems to be known about periodic domains which are not recurrent. (ii) If Omega is not recurrent, does there exist P ∈ ∂Omega such that limk→∞ f nk (Q) = P for all Q ∈ Omega? (iii) If Omega is not recurrent, does there exist P ∈ ∂Omega such that f n P = P , and one of the eigenvalues of DF (P ) is e2πip/q ?

evidence.quote: Problem 12.3.2 (New) A diffeomorphism between two strongly pseudoconvex CR (2n + 1)-manifolds is called quasiconformal if its differential preserves the underlying contact structures and distorts the CR structures boundedly.
